title: Modify the Matrix
statement: You are given an `m x n` integer grid `matrix`. Build and return a new grid `answer` of the same size that copies `matrix` cell by cell, except that every cell holding `-1` is filled with the largest value found anywhere in that cell's column of `matrix`. Every column is guaranteed to contain at least one non-negative number.
constraints: Each column contains at least one non-negative value
notes:
## Intuition

Every `-1` in a column is replaced by the same number, the column's maximum. Looking up that maximum again for each `-1` would rescan the column every time (O(m² · n) at worst). Instead, scan each column once to find its maximum, then make a second pass down the same column to fill the holes.

Because every column has a non-negative value, the maximum is never `-1` itself, so starting the running maximum at `-1` is safe.

## Approach

1. Copy `matrix` row by row into `answer` so the input stays untouched.
2. For each column `col`, set `columnMax` to `-1` and walk all rows, keeping the largest value.
3. Walk the same column again and overwrite every `-1` in `answer` with `columnMax`.
4. Return `answer`.

## Example 1, step by step

`matrix = [[1,2,-1],[4,-1,6],[7,8,9]]`.

- Column 0 holds `1, 4, 7`: `columnMax = 7`, no `-1` to fill.
- Column 1 holds `2, -1, 8`: `columnMax = 8`, so `answer[1][1]` becomes `8`.
- Column 2 holds `-1, 6, 9`: `columnMax = 9`, so `answer[0][2]` becomes `9`.

The result is `[[1,2,9],[4,8,6],[7,8,9]]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n): each cell is read twice.
- Space: O(m · n) for the returned copy; O(1) extra besides it.

## Pitfalls

- The maximum is per **column**, not per row; mixing up `row` and `col` indices is the usual bug.
- Fill only after the whole column is scanned: filling during the scan would use the maximum of the rows seen so far, which is too small when a bigger value sits lower down.
- Copy each row (`[...row]`); `matrix.slice()` alone shares the inner arrays with the input.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `m`, `n` | number of rows and columns |
| `answer` | the copied grid that is filled and returned |
| `col`, `row` | the current column and row indices |
| `columnMax` | the largest value in column `col` |

narration.4: Copy every row so the input matrix is not changed.
narration.6: Handle the grid one column at a time.
narration.7: Start the column's maximum at -1; a real value will always beat it.
narration.8: First pass: walk down the column.
narration.9: Keep the largest value seen in this column.
narration.11: Second pass: walk down the same column again.
narration.13: Yes: replace it with the column's maximum.
narration.17: Every column is filled; return the new grid.
